chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from some of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام:
Regarding a man who broke another man’s hand, then the man’s hand healed, he عليه السلام said: “There is no qiṣāṣ in this, but al-arsh is to be given.”

key_terms.الْأَرْشَ: assessed financial compensation for bodily injury
key_terms.قِصَاصٌ: retaliatory legal punishment equal to the injury
key_terms.كَسَرَ: broke; caused a fracture or breakage
key_terms.يَدَ: hand; the injured limb in this ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone breaks another person’s hand and it later heals?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning bodily injury when a hand is broken but later heals. It states that qiṣāṣ does not apply in this case; instead, financial compensation in the form of al-arsh is awarded.
